mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% within the last month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence rise.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and related sectors benefit.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% over the same period, it signals a robust demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3%, it signals a favorable economic environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 0.5% in 1 quarter and FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.
